topic.title: SAT Data Analysis
topic.description: College Readiness / SAT-style items (Problem-Solving and Data Analysis).

questions.problem:
A school club with 80 members, equally divided among freshmen, sophomores, juniors, and seniors, reported attendance at a workshop. 5 freshmen, 8 sophomores, 10 juniors, and 12 seniors attended. If a club member who attended the workshop is selected at random, what is the probability they are a senior?

Options:
A) $\frac{12}{80}$
B) $\frac{12}{35}$
C) $\frac{12}{23}$
D) $\frac{12}{20}$
questions.explanation: I was between a 2 and a 3 because the "equally divided..." part is extraneous and therefore this question includes minor details that could distract the student.
questions.hint: Skill: Probability and conditional probability

I rated the vocab a 3 because you'd have to create something to plug into or make a table, so the plugging in part would include a mathematical step created by the test taker.

questions.problem:
A school counselor wants to determine if increasing nightly sleep causes higher math test scores. After a month, the sleep extension group scored significantly higher on average. Can the counselor conclude that increased sleep causes higher scores?

Options:
A) No, because other factors could influence test scores.
B) No, because the students were not randomly sampled from the population.
C) Yes, because the groups were randomly assigned.

questions.answer: Yes, because the groups were randomly assigned.
questions.explanation: I have a problem with the conclusive nature of the language in this problem.
